entries.title: EIA power plant generation FAQ
entries.pinned_paraphrase: In the EIA example, a single 100 MW generator running continuously at that capacity for 24 hours generates 2,400 MWh. Operating continuously at that capacity for 365 days would generate 876,000 MWh.

entries.title: EIA glossary capacity factor
entries.pinned_paraphrase: Capacity factor divides a generating unit’s actual electrical energy output for a given period by the electrical energy it could have generated by running at full power throughout that same period.
